Our Client is a fast-growing procurement and technology company headquartered in Riyadh with operations across Saudi Arabia and Bahrain. We are building innovative solutions to simplify procurement processes, empower businesses, and create meaningful impact.

Why Join Us?

We are looking for talented, growth-minded individuals eager to take on new challenges. We nurture potential and provide an environment where every employee can thrive professionally and personally.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you'll be a key technical leader, driving the design, development, and maintenance of our core backend services. You'll collaborate extensively with product, frontend, and DevOps teams to architect and build highly scalable, efficient, and robust systems. Your contributions will directly enable our customers to optimize their procurement workflows and derive critical insights. This role demands a deep focus on crafting resilient APIs, optimizing database structures, and building seamless integration services that significantly enhance system performance and user experience.

What You'll Do:

● Lead System Architecture: Spearhead the architectural design of backend systems, ensuring they are secure, reliable, high-performance, and align with our long-term technical vision.
● Develop Scalable Solutions: Design and implement sophisticated backend services, APIs, and microservices for our advanced procure-to-pay platform.

● Integrate and Innovate: Drive integrations with critical third-party systems, including enterprise-grade ERPs like Oracle Fusion, to expand our platform's capabilities.

● Troubleshoot and Evolve: Proactively identify, troubleshoot, and resolve complex issues in existing backend systems, implementing upgrades and enhancements to continuously improve performance and scalability.

● Mentor and Elevate: Provide technical leadership and mentorship to junior developers, championing best practices through rigorous code reviews and knowledge sharing.

● Ensure Operational Excellence: Implement comprehensive monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions to guarantee the health, reliability, and proactive management of our systems.

● Strategic Contribution: Play a pivotal role in strategic decisions regarding backend architecture, technology stack selections, and future platform evolution.

What You'll Bring:

● Extensive Backend Expertise: Strong hands-on experience as a MEAN Stack Developer with a proven track record of building and scaling complex backend systems.

● Distributed Systems Mastery: Deep experience building distributed and scalable backend infrastructure with a microservices-first design philosophy.

● API Design Proficiency: In-depth understanding and practical experience with RESTful API design and microservice architectures.

● Core Technologies: Proficient in Node.js, Express.js or Nest.js, with a solid grasp of building REST APIs, Websockets, SQL/NoSQL Databases (MongoDB), message queues, distributed caches, and data pipelines.

● Problem-Solving Acumen: Exceptional troubleshooting, debugging, and performance tuning skills. Nice to Have:

● Experience with GCP deployments and pipeline management.

● Prior experience integrating with external systems, especially ERPs.

● Familiarity with AI/ML concepts and their application in backend services.

● Knowledge of monorepos and tools like Nx.dev.

item.description:
Headquarters: Beirut, Lebanon
URL: http://jobsforhumanity.com

Company Description

AB Group PLLC is a dynamic architecture firm with a passion for delivering innovative and impactful designs. Specializing in hospitality, multifamily, and office projects, we take pride in creating spaces that inspire. We are expanding our talented team and looking for a skilled Autodesk Revit Draftsperson to join us remotely from Lebanon.

Job Description

Position Overview

ABG is seeking a highly responsive, articulate, and results-driven Appointment Setter and HubSpot CRM Manager.
This person will be responsible for contacting new inbound leads within 60 seconds of:

  • Submitting a contact form through the ABG website.
  • Calling ABG’s front desk line.
  • Leaving a voicemail or missed call.
  • Entering ABG’s lead system through another marketing channel.
  • This position requires an exceptionally high sense of urgency. Every minute of delay reduces the likelihood of connecting with and converting a prospective client.
  • The successful candidate must have impeccable spoken and written English, a confident telephone presence, strong listening skills, and the ability to communicate professionally with business owners, developers, contractors, investors, property owners, and other decision-makers.
  • The role also includes cold calling and cold emailing targeted contact lists to create new relationships and generate opportunities in specific geographic and industry markets.

Core Responsibilities

Inbound Lead Response

  • Monitor website inquiries, phone calls, voicemails, emails, and assigned lead notifications throughout working hours.
  • Call every new website lead within 60 seconds of form submission.
  • Return every missed front desk call within 60 seconds of receiving the notification.
  • Answer live calls promptly and professionally whenever assigned to front desk coverage.
  • Send an immediate follow-up email when a lead does not answer.
  • Continue following up through an organized call and email cadence until the lead:
  • Responds.
  • Schedules an appointment.
  • Requests future follow-up.
  • Is confirmed as unqualified.
  • Opts out of further communication.
  • Never allow an inbound lead to sit in HubSpot without a documented response attempt and scheduled next action.

Lead Qualification

  • Conduct an effective initial conversation to understand:
  • Prospect name, company, and contact information.
  • Project address and geographic location.
  • Project type and intended use.
  • Requested architectural, engineering, interior design, permitting, or consulting services.
  • Current project status.
  • Estimated project size and scope.
  • Target schedule.
  • Preliminary construction or design budget.
  • Property ownership or site-control status.
  • Decision-makers involved.
  • How the prospect heard about ABG.
  • Identify whether the opportunity is aligned with ABG’s services and target markets.
  • Ask clear and direct questions without making the prospect feel interrogated.
  • Avoid providing technical, legal, pricing, or code-related advice beyond the approved qualification script.
  • Escalate urgent, high-value, or strategically important opportunities immediately.
  • Appointment Setting
  • Schedule qualified prospects with the correct ABG team member.
  • Confirm the appointment date, time, meeting format, project address, and attendee information.
  • Send calendar invitations and confirmation messages immediately.
  • Send appointment reminders to improve attendance.
  • Reschedule cancelled or missed appointments quickly.
  • Ensure the assigned ABG team member has complete qualification notes before the meeting.
  • Follow up after the appointment when directed and update the opportunity status in HubSpot.

HubSpot CRM Management

  • Serve as the day-to-day owner of sales data quality in HubSpot.
  • Create and maintain accurate:
  • Contact records.
  • Company records.
  • Deal records.
  • Lead-source information.
  • Deal stages.
  • Activity records.
  • Follow-up tasks.
  • Appointment records.
  • Log every call, voicemail, email, response, qualification note, appointment, and follow-up action.
  • Ensure every open lead has:
  • A clearly assigned owner.
  • The correct pipeline stage.
  • Complete contact information.
  • A documented last activity.
  • A scheduled next action.
  • A realistic follow-up date.
  • Move deals through ABG’s sales pipeline based on verified activity:
  • First Contact.
  • Discovery.
  • Send Fee.
  • Fee Sent.
  • Standby.
  • Accepted.
  • Send Contract.
  • Contract Sent.
  • Project Won or Project Lost.
  • Prevent duplicate contacts, companies, and deals.
  • Standardize naming conventions and correct incomplete or inaccurate records.
  • Identify stale deals, overdue tasks, missing follow-ups, and opportunities without recent activity.
  • Maintain lead lists, call queues, workflows, templates, sequences, and reporting dashboards.
  • Produce daily and weekly reports covering:
  • New inbound leads.
  • Average response time.
  • Leads contacted within 60 seconds.
  • Contact rate.
  • Qualified leads.
  • Appointments scheduled.
  • Appointment attendance rate.
  • Outbound calls and emails.
  • New relationships created.
  • Pipeline-stage movement.
  • Stale or neglected opportunities.
  • CRM data-quality issues.
  • Cold Calling and Cold Emailing

Conduct structured outbound campaigns targeting ABG’s priority markets.

  • Call and email prospective:
  • Real estate developers.
  • General contractors.
  • Commercial property owners.
  • Real estate investors.
  • Brokers and tenant representatives.
  • Property managers.
  • Franchise owners and operators.
  • Restaurant and hospitality groups.
  • Retail and industrial businesses.
  • Multifamily and residential developers.
  • Strategic referral partners.
  • Research contacts and verify names, titles, companies, telephone numbers, email addresses, locations, and market relevance.
  • Use approved scripts and email templates while keeping conversations natural and personalized.
  • Introduce ABG’s capabilities clearly and confidently.
  • Focus on building relationships, identifying upcoming projects, and securing introductory meetings.
  • Handle common objections professionally and continue the conversation without becoming aggressive.
  • Document all outbound activity and prospect responses in HubSpot.
  • Create follow-up tasks for every viable prospect.
  • Maintain organized prospect lists by market, relationship type, campaign, and opportunity status.
  • Provide feedback on which industries, messages, and contact lists generate the strongest results.

Non-Negotiable Performance Standards

  • Demonstrate an exceptional sense of urgency at all times.
  • Contact new inbound leads within 60 seconds during assigned coverage hours.
  • Maintain impeccable spoken and written English.
  • Communicate clearly without grammatical errors, excessive filler words, slang, or an unprofessional tone.
  • Remain available and attentive during scheduled lead-response coverage.
  • Treat every inbound inquiry as a time-sensitive potential client.
  • Complete CRM updates immediately after each interaction.
  • Never rely on memory or personal notes in place of HubSpot documentation.
  • Never leave a lead without a clearly documented next action.
  • Follow through on commitments without repeated reminders.
  • Maintain a polished, confident, helpful, and professional demeanor.
  • Protect confidential client, project, and company information.
  • Key Performance Indicators

Percentage of inbound leads called within 60 seconds.

  • Average first-response time.
  • Inbound lead contact rate.
  • Qualified-lead rate.
  • Appointment-setting rate.
  • Appointment attendance rate.
  • Missed appointment recovery rate.
  • Number of outbound calls completed.
  • Number of personalized outbound emails sent.
  • Outbound contact and response rate.
  • Number of qualified outbound appointments scheduled.
  • Number of new strategic relationships created.
  • Percentage of CRM records with complete required information.
  • Percentage of open opportunities with a scheduled next activity.
  • Number of stale or overdue opportunities.
  • Accuracy and timeliness of daily and weekly reports.
  • Required Qualifications

Exceptional spoken and written English.

  • Clear, confident, and professional telephone voice.
  • Strong listening, questioning, and note-taking skills.
  • Demonstrated success in appointment setting, inside sales, lead qualification, business development, or customer service.
  • Experience using HubSpot CRM or a comparable CRM platform.
  • Ability to learn ABG’s services, target markets, qualification criteria, and sales process.
  • Ability to work quickly without sacrificing accuracy or professionalism.
  • Strong organizational skills and consistent attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage a high volume of calls, emails, tasks, and records.
  • Comfortable speaking with senior decision-makers and business owners.
  • Ability to handle rejection and objections without losing momentum.
  • Reliable internet, telephone access, and a professional work environment if working remotely.

 

    Qualifications

    Preferred Qualifications

    • Experience managing HubSpot contacts, companies, deals, tasks, lists, workflows, sequences, and reports.
    • Experience in architecture, engineering, construction, commercial real estate, professional services, or a related industry.
    • Experience with business-to-business cold calling and email outreach.
    • Familiarity with calendar scheduling, email platforms, contact databases, and list-building tools.
    • Experience qualifying projects involving architecture, engineering, permitting, construction, development, or property improvements.

    Personal Characteristics

    • Urgent and highly responsive.
    • Persistent without being pushy.
    • Organized and process-oriented.
    • Competitive and motivated by measurable results.
    • Comfortable being held accountable to activity and conversion targets.
    • Professional under pressure.
    • Coachable and receptive to call reviews and feedback.
    • Proactive in identifying problems and recommending improvements.
    • Consistent, dependable, and disciplined.
    • Focused on creating an excellent first impression of ABG.

    What Success Looks Like

    • Prospective clients are contacted while their interest is at its highest.
    • Every lead receives fast, professional, and persistent follow-up.
    • Qualified prospects are consistently converted into scheduled appointments.
    • ABG’s HubSpot pipeline is accurate, current, and easy for leadership to manage.
    • No viable opportunity is lost because of slow response, poor communication, or missing follow-up.
    • Outbound campaigns create measurable new relationships and qualified opportunities in ABG’s target markets.
    • ABG’s leadership receives reliable reporting and has complete visibility into every active prospect and next action.

    Candidate Evaluation

    • A mock inbound lead-response call.
    • A cold-call role-play.

    Additional Information

Rebill rates erode quickly past month one. Add-on attach is minimal. Our reactivation engine is currently offline. We've been operating an email-only CRM on a platform that doesn't return analytics through its API.

That ends with this hire. This is a role for someone who has already done the transformation we need: turning a basic broadcast CRM into a measurable CVM function that drives incremental revenue across email, SMS, and web push — on the US market specifically.

What You'll Own

Funnel Conversion

  • Drive Reg→Purchase conversion through triggered post-quiz, paywall-abandonment, and onboarding sequences across email, SMS, and web push.
  • Own first-purchase activation across the first 7 days.

Retention & Rebill

  • Differentiate renewal sequences by plan tier (1 / 3 / 6 month).
  • Build pre-cancel intervention flows — pause offer, plan-switch, value reminder — using captured cancel reason.
  • Move the dial on month-1 rebill rate, the single most leveraged metric in our subscription economics.

Reactivation

  • Build the reactivation engine for the cancelled cohort — across email and SMS, personalized by cancel reason and tenure.
  • Recover revenue from a base that is currently dormant due to deliverability issues.

Add-on Monetization

  • Own the CRM-driven path to add-on products (Resume Review, Resume Builder): timing, segmentation, copy, channel.

Channel & Tooling

  • Lead the migration off our current ESP onto our chosen omnichannel platform (Maestra is the current candidate; Customer.io is the alternative).
  • Recover and maintain email domain reputation.
  • Stand up SMS as a first-class channel — including US compliance (TCPA, A2P 10DLC).
  • Stand up web push and orchestrate cross-channel flows (email → SMS → push cascades).

Measurement

  • Implement incremental measurement with holdouts on every flow. We don't want activity reports — we want incremental revenue, attributable and defensible.

Expected Outcomes

First 3 Months

  1. Email deliverability restored to historical baseline.
  2. Reactivation campaign launched with measurable incremental conversion against a holdout.
  3. Differentiated renewal flows live for 1 / 3 / 6 month plans.
  4. Decision (signed off with engineering) on omnichannel platform: migrate to Maestra or alternative.

First 6 Months

  1. SMS and web push live as ongoing production channels in lifecycle flows.
  2. Measurable lift in Reg→Purchase conversion via paywall-abandonment and post-registration triggered sequences.
  3. Measurable lift in month-1 rebill rate via differentiated and intervention flows.
  4. Add-on attach rate (Resume Review, Resume Builder) materially up via CRM-driven sales sequences.
  5. Per-flow incremental revenue reported weekly via proper holdout methodology.

12 Months

  1. CVM channel contributing as a top-3 incremental revenue source for the company.
  2. Cross-channel lifecycle strategy (email + SMS + web push + iMessage/RCS as those channels mature in the US) live and documented.
  3. Process documentation and tooling stable enough to remove key-person risk.


We keep our hiring process quick and simple:

Requirements

You're a Fit If You Have

  • 3+ years operating CVM/lifecycle programs on the US market specifically. US b2c subscription. This is non-negotiable — US deliverability, US carriers, US consumer behavior, US compliance.
  • 5+ years total in CRM / lifecycle / CVM, with at least one stint owning the function end-to-end (not just executing).

  • SQL good enough to pull your own segments and validate your own data.

  • Direct work with the CMO, CEO, and Growth PM. No layers, no politics.

The role

We are hiring a technical customer support person with an owner's mentality.

You will own support for QuickMail and Mailflow, our deliverability add-on. There is no first or second line. You are the first and last person our customers talk to.

Customers count on you to solve their problems and find the real cause when something breaks. You work closely with engineering, and you tell the founder what we need to know to make the product better: where the friction is and where the opportunities are.

The role covers the help desk, system health checks, testing new releases before they ship, and leading the weekly team meeting. It takes excellent communication, solid technical understanding and sharp critical thinking.

This is not a script-reading job. Most tickets involve deliverability, DNS records, LinkedIn automation or campaign setup. You dig into customer accounts in our Support Dashboard, reproduce the issue, then decide what to do and how to explain it to the customer.

We are a remote team spread across time zones. Most routine tasks have a written guide with a checklist, so you know what done looks like. You are expected to refine and improve those processes. When something new comes up, you work out the most efficient way to handle it.

If you want a lot of autonomy across many areas, real responsibility and a fast-paced environment, this role is for you.

 

What work looks like

You own two things: customers get unstuck fast, and the product stays reliable

 

Every day

  • ⁠Set the day's support priorities and work the Help Scout queue for QuickMail and Mailflow. Triage, resolve, and dig deeper when a ticket needs it.
  • ⁠Check the support dashboard: job queue, event-stream latency, blacklist status, newly purchased domains. If something is off, investigate, diagnose, and drive it to resolution.
  • ⁠Review fraud alerts and disable accounts that are scams or abusing the platform.

 

Delighting customers

  • Comfortable jumping on calls with customers, building rapport fast. and set them up for success.
  • ⁠Update the changelog and help articles based on what shipped and what customers asked.
  • ⁠Share customer feedback with the team, ask happy customers for reviews and case studies, and watch NPS for testimonial candidates.

 

Making support smarter with AI

  • ⁠Improve the AI support agent. Review its answers, fix the docs it drew from when it is wrong, and contact the customer when its reply was off.
  • Write and maintain automated tests, built with AI, that try to break staging before customers do.
  • ⁠Use the MCP connections we have in place (Helpscout, GitHub, Postmark, and others) to get an accurate picture of support and find the next thing worth improving.

 

Keeping the product solid

  • ⁠Gatekeep releases. New fixes and features land on staging every week. Test them, confirm when staging is ready to ship, and think through how existing and new users will be affected.
  • Report bugs as GitHub issues with everything the developer needs: steps to reproduce, screenshots or a Loom, and any GraphQL or console errors.
  • ⁠Captain red alerts. When a core feature breaks (emails not sending, login down), confirm it, alert the team on Slack or Telegram, update the status page every 30 minutes, keep affected customers informed, and drive the fix. Then run the retrospective so it does not happen twice.

 

Running the week

  • ⁠Lead the weekly team meeting in MonsterOps: issues written up, to-dos done, numbers updated.
  • ⁠Keep rock status and KPIs current in MonsterOps.

 

Tools you'll use: Helpscout, our Support Dashboard, Sidekiq, GitHub, Slack, Telegram, MonsterOps, Outline, MxToolbox, Postmark, Bento, TidyCal, Fathom, Visual Code and Claude.

Requirements

Who you are

  • You build rapport fast. You are warm, positive, and relatable in writing and on calls.
  • You are a good communicator. Externally, you can show warmth, empathy and care. Internally, you are able to communicate clearly and concisely about important things.
  • You can operate with minimal instructions. You understand a short brief without every detail spelled out. You can prioritize well (especially when you have a lot on your plate), and get things done without hand-holding.
  • You are comfortable on video. You are natural on live calls with Zoom and Meet, and on recorded video through tools like loom.
  • Your teammates can always count on you. You say what you'll do and you do what you said.
  • You act with a constant sense of urgency. You can execute fast and find new ways to improve your productivity.
  • You are resourceful. You use all the tools at your disposal to get great results.
  • You have a low ego. You don't take offense easily and you handle disagreement as a discussion, not a personal attack.
  • Growth mindset. You are positive about new workflow/process/product/tool changes. You love giving and receiving positive and negative feedback without getting defensive.
  • Hours that overlap with East coast US and UK, where most of our customers are.

 

A plus if you have

  • Have experience with customer facing, or if you don't have it, tell us why you are perfect for this role.
  • Working knowledge of deliverability and LinkedIn outreach. Warmup, DNS, inbox rotation, DKIM, SPF, Outlook and Gmail technical setup, . We can teach this, but a head start helps.
  • Comfort with agency setups. Workspaces, guest seats, inbox purchases and what happens when an agency loses a client.
  • Light data skills. You can pull numbers from Help Scout or our MCP to back up what you report.
  • An eye for happy customers. You notice them and ask for testimonials and case studies at the right moment.

 

How we work together

You’ll work directly with me, the founder, and with our lead developer.

Working with me can be intense. Here is what that looks like in practice:

  • My replies are short and can come across as harsh. If something I wrote lands badly or isn’t clear, ask me.
  • My direction can change. I may say one thing, then something different a few days later as I learn more. When that happens, check what changed and adapt.
  • I prefer information to be short and to the point. Lead with what matters, then give more details if I ask.
  • I can stay frustrated about a problem until it’s solved. That's something I'm aware of and working on. You’ll do well here if you can stay calm and focused when the pressure is on.
  • We often think fast and interrupt each other when discussing ideas. If that would bother you, this role probably isn’t for you.

 

This role suits someone with high emotional intelligence, who doesn’t take things personally, asks when something is unclear, and keeps many things moving at once.

Your schedule can be flexible. If you have a martial arts class every Thursday at 3 pm, go and make up the time later. In return, on the rare occasion we need your help on a weekend, we ask you to be flexible too.

  1. Customer Retention: The percentage of customers you successfully retain within your assigned portfolio.

item.description:

At Mixmax, we're building the future of how revenue teams work: smarter, faster, and more human. Our platform helps teams stay on top of every conversation by automating busywork, delivering real-time insights, and integrating with the tools they already use.

We're hiring a Billing Support Analyst in the Philippines to join our small but mighty team as one of the go-to contributors and resources for how our customers are billed. You'll resolve billing questions from start to finish, dig into the technical issues that sit underneath them, and keep our Stripe records accurate to the cent. It's part customer support, part billing operations, and part detective work.

This role reports directly to our Billing Team Lead, who reports into Head of Customer Experience. You'll work closely with Customer Support, Customer Success, Sales and Engineering across global time zones (NAMER, LATAM, EU), and you'll help shape how we use AI and automation to make billing faster and more accurate for customers.

If you check that an invoice's line items add up to its total before you read the customer's email, keep reading.

Outcomes

In your first 3 months

  • Learn Mixmax's plans, pricing, billing policies and Stripe setup well enough to resolve standard billing tickets on your own.
  • Own a share of the billing queue in Intercom (refunds, invoice questions, plan and seat changes, cancellations) with accurate, on-time responses.
  • Troubleshoot the technical side of billing tickets, such as seat assignment, workspace access and plan-status issues, before escalating.
  • Take over daily past-due invoice follow-up and payment-failure handling.
  • Become a reliable backup for the Billing Team Lead, so billing keeps moving when anyone is out.
  • Use AI tools day to day to summarize ticket history, draft replies and check your work, with every number verified by hand, and find new efficiencies for the team.

In your first 6 months

  • Handle complex cases on your own: invoice disputes, proration questions, credits, and billing setup for sales-led contracts.
  • Run recurring reconciliations between Stripe, Salesforce and our product data, and flag mismatches before customers notice them.
  • Write and update billing macros, help-center articles and internal process docs
  • Help test and roll out billing automation, including AI-assisted ticket handling, and define which billing actions should stay with a human.
  • Contribute at least one reusable AI or automation workflow to the team, such as an invoice-dispute triage prompt or a reconciliation checklist.

What you'll own

  • Accurate, timely resolution of customer billing inquiries from first reply to close.
  • Stripe account hygiene: invoices, subscriptions, credits, refunds and payment issues.
  • Past-due invoice collection and failed-payment follow-up.
  • Billing accuracy checks and reconciliations across our systems.
  • Clear documentation of billing processes, so knowledge doesn't live in one person's head

What you'll be doing

  • Answer billing questions in our support queue, explaining charges, proration and plan changes in plain language
  • Diagnose the technical issues behind billing tickets, like a seat that is billed but not in use or a user stuck on the wrong plan, and work with Support and Engineering to fix them
  • Prepare, correct and send invoices; process refunds, credits and cancellations within policy
  • Spot patterns in billing tickets and turn them into fixes, process changes or product feedback
  • Use AI and automation to work faster, while knowing where accuracy, privacy and customer trust require a human
  • Take on ad-hoc analysis and projects that keep billing records correct

What we're looking for

  • 3+ years of combined experience in technical customer support and billing support (invoicing, payments, refunds, collections). You need hands-on experience in both.
  • Experience at a technology or SaaS company
  • Hands-on experience with Stripe and/or accounting and billing software (e.g., QuickBooks, Xero, Chargebee, Zuora, NetSuite)
  • You are very strong with numbers. Proration, percentages, discounts and reconciliations come easily to you, and you check your math without being asked.
  • You are meticulous. You catch the wrong date, the duplicate line and the typo in an email domain.
  • Working knowledge of AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or AI features in support tools). You can explain how you use them, how you check their output, and what you won't put into them.
  • Fluent written and spoken English. You can explain a complicated invoice to a frustrated customer clearly and kindly.
  • Based in the Philippines, with a reliable home setup and a schedule that overlaps North American business hours (we'll agree on it together).
  • Comfortable in a remote, fast-moving organization where processes are still being built and refined.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Intercom, Zendesk or a similar support platform, and with Salesforce
  • Background in accounting, finance or bookkeeping
  • Experience with subscription or usage-based billing models
  • Comfort with spreadsheets beyond the basics (lookups, pivots) or light SQL

Core competencies

  • Numeracy: Fast, accurate reasoning with money, dates and percentages
  • Accuracy & detail: Gets it right the first time and catches what others miss
  • Billing operations: Knows how invoices, subscriptions, proration, refunds and collections actually work
  • ️ Technical troubleshooting: Separates a billing problem from a product problem and finds the root cause
  • AI fluency & judgment: Uses AI to go faster and knows when not to
  • Clear, calm communication: Turns confusing charges into answers customers trust
  • ️ Judgment & integrity: Applies policy fairly, escalates the right things, and treats customer money with care

Why Mixmax?

  • Remote-first with async-friendly workflows and a globally distributed team.
  • A product with strong market fit and a loyal, engaged customer base.
  • A culture that values autonomy, quality, innovation and momentum.
  • Competitive compensation and flexible time off.
  • An inclusive, thoughtful team that values long-term success for customers and for each other.

Our commitment to diversity and inclusion

At Mixmax, we know that nobody's perfect and that no one ever matches 100% of a job description. That's okay. Diversity and inclusion are core to our culture, and we're committed to building a more inclusive and open workplace. No matter your background or how you identify, if you're excited about this role, please apply.

You will also own shared inbound customer channels, ensuring questions and requests are triaged, resolved, or routed to the right partner with clear follow-through.

The successful candidate is a customer-focused operator who is equally comfortable analyzing a portfolio, building repeatable engagement programs, writing clear customer communications, and speaking directly with customers to understand their experience. You will bring recent experience managing or materially influencing customer renewals, including the ability to interpret retention metrics, identify churn and contraction risk, execute save plays, and surface customer-backed growth levers.   • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create clear customer-facing content and lead effective discovery or feedback conversations.

Preferred Qualifications

Dropbox isn’t just a workplace—it’s a living lab for designing a more enlightened way of working. We’re a global community of bold visionaries and resourceful doers shaping the future of Dropbox and, in turn, the future of work. Our Virtual First model combines the autonomy of a distributed workplace with the power of human connection, creating space for meaningful work and lasting relationships. With a startup mindset and enterprise-level opportunities, we expect Dropbox employees to think critically, stay curious, and use modern tools, including AI, to improve how work gets done. Here, you can be who you are and grow into who you’re meant to be. You own your impact, helping make work more intuitive, joyful, and human for yourself and hundreds of millions of people worldwide. If you’re ready to push boundaries and challenge yourself, Dropbox is ready for you.

The Dropbox Customer Experience and Success (CXS) Team shapes how more than 700 million users and 575k teams worldwide interact with our products. We turn insights into actions, bringing empathy and expertise to every touchpoint. Our team embraces resourcefulness and curiosity, pushing boundaries—and ourselves—to improve the customer experience and ensure our customers achieve their desired outcomes with our products, leading to increased customer lifetime value, retention, and growth. Dropbox’s Virtual First way of working is designed to help people do their best work with flexibility, autonomy, and connection. Day to day, teams work remotely with nonlinear schedules and core collaboration hours that support deep focus and individual working styles. We prioritize asynchronous communication to improve clarity, respect deep work time, and reduce unnecessary meetings. While remote work is the primary experience for our employees, we also prioritize intentional, in-person connection. AI fluency is a core part of how we work and grow. It’s not about being an expert—it’s about using these tools thoughtfully and effectively to improve your work and support others.

  • Leverage: You use AI to enhance thinking, improve efficiency, and increase your impact and your team’s.
  • Learning: You stay current on emerging AI tools and trends, continuously build your skills, and share what you learn with others.
 
Together, these behaviors help build a workforce where technology amplifies human judgment, creativity, and impact.

item.title: Town Web: Senior Support Engineer
item.description:

URL: https://townweb.com

Senior Support Engineer

Town Web · HeyGov · ClerkMinutes. Remote, Central US hours. $85,000 to $105,000 a year. Open to candidates in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland.

About us

We make municipal software built for clerks: websites residents can use, forms and payments that replace stacks of paper, and meeting minutes drafted after every meeting. More than 1,300 local governments rely on us, from counties and cities to villages and towns. We have local government clients in almost every state in the U.S.

Our clients are municipal clerks and the government teams around them. They keep city hall running and rarely get thanked for it. Your job is to make working with us the easy part of their week.

The role

This is the senior seat on our Client Success team. We are hiring you to raise the standard of our support: fix what is broken, write down how it should work, and show what great looks like.

Our AI agent now answers repeatable, well-documented questions. What is left is the work that only a person can do: own a client's problem from the first message to the confirmed fix, build a relationship a clerk trusts, and turn what you learn into better documentation and a better product.

This is not a ticket-closing job. Think of a great 5-star hotel that puts slippers by the bed before you ask. We want a clerk to finish a conversation with you and tell the clerk in the next town about the great experience they had. If that takes three calls, take three calls.

It is also a technical job. You will work with our developers every day. When something breaks, you work out where it lives before anyone else has to. Is the problem on the events calendar on the client's homepage, or in the calendar widget embedded on a department page? Is the wrong speaker name only in the transcript, or is it also in the finished minutes? You reproduce it, write it up so a developer can act without a follow-up question, stay on it until it ships, and tell the client yourself.

You need both halves. A brilliant troubleshooter who is short with a clerk will not work here. Neither will a lovely person who forwards every problem to a developer.

Your first 90 days

  • Learn all of our products well enough to teach them
  • Take over every open escalation and close or schedule each one
  • Rebuild the path from support to our developers so nothing leaves the queue untracked
  • Find the ten questions clerks ask most and fix each at the source: an article, a Fin answer, or a product change

What you will do

Raise the standard

  • Design how issues move from support to developers, and keep that path working
  • Set the bar for replies, calls, and write-ups, and coach teammates by example
  • Turn what you fix into playbooks the team and Fin can follow

Delight clients

  • Make every interaction feel personal, warm, and unhurried, especially for less technical users who would rather talk to a person than read a help article
  • Step in when the AI agent or the documentation is not enough, and make sure the client feels heard and helped, not processed
  • Treat client sentiment as the real measure of success, not ticket speed
  • Look for small moments to go above and beyond, and share what works so it becomes how the whole team operates

Own the problem from start to finish

  • Be the named person on an account when things go wrong: one owner, one plan, regular updates, until the client says it is fixed
  • Step in early when an account shows strain (repeat tickets, a rough launch, a frustrated message) and run the recovery. Get on a call, write down what is open, set dates, follow through
  • Make sure nothing sits untracked once it leaves the support queue

Diagnose, then escalate

  • Work out which product and which layer an issue lives in before you hand it to a developer
  • Reproduce it, capture the steps with screenshots or a recording, and file it in Linear with everything a developer needs
  • Check on your open Linear issues, chase what is stuck, and confirm the fix with the client
  • Use Claude, connected to our code repository, to trace where a behavior comes from. For small, well-understood fixes, draft the change for a developer to review

Knowledge base and AI support

  • Inherit and maintain the help center for all of our products. It is what our AI agent (Fin, in Intercom) answers from
  • Write and improve articles from real, recurring questions, on a weekly rhythm measured against live ticket volume
  • Write troubleshooting guides that separate look-alike problems, so the next person, or Fin, can tell them apart
  • Tune Fin: review where it failed, fix the article, and teach it to ask a clarifying question when a request could mean two things
  • Record short training videos so clients can learn at their own pace

Support and onboarding

  • Handle the conversations Fin cannot resolve across Town Web (websites), HeyGov (forms, payments, reservations, campaigns), and ClerkMinutes (agendas, transcripts, minutes)
  • Help new clients through onboarding with the projects team so they reach value quickly
  • Talk with clerks by phone and video every week. Get on a call whenever a situation needs a human voice

Account care

  • Build real relationships with your assigned accounts
  • Understand what each client is trying to accomplish, what they use, what they do not know we offer, and where they will need help before they ask
  • Run proactive, recurring check-ins instead of waiting for tickets. For example, reach out a few weeks after go-live to review how their forms are performing
  • Use product usage data to spot clients who are not getting full value yet
  • Meet clients in person. Join us at clerk conferences and marketing events a few times a year. We cover all travel & lodging expenses

Spot opportunity

  • Tell clients about services they do not use yet (digital forms, payments, .gov domains, accessibility, training) without it feeling like a pitch
  • Flag possible expansion and renewal opportunities to the sales team

Training

  • Get clients to real proficiency with the product, not just past their immediate question
  • Work with Product Managers to co-host webinars about new features and training

Tools you will use: Intercom and Fin, Linear, Claude, our help center, screen recording, Zoom phone.

How we work

  • Delight over deflection. The goal is happy, successful clients, not fewer conversations
  • Ownership over routing. A hard case is yours until it is resolved
  • Diagnose before you escalate. A developer should never have to ask what the client actually saw
  • Documentation is the foundation everything else runs on, not an afterthought
  • Teaching over ticket-closing. Proficiency, not just an answer

Who you are

  • You like people, and it shows. Clerks are often not technical, sometimes stressed, and now and then upset. You pick up the phone gladly and leave them calmer than you found them
  • Hospitable by nature. A background in hospitality or another service-first field is a plus
  • You have done support somewhere known for it. The standard we have in mind is Basecamp: competent, calm, and trusted to make the call
  • Technically deep. You read the error, open the browser console and the network tab, check a DNS record, find your way around WordPress, and follow the trail into the code with Claude's help
  • At home with developers. You know what a good bug report contains and you have filed plenty
  • High autonomy. You decide, act, and report. You do not wait to be told
  • A clear, warm, precise writer, with clients and across teams
  • A natural teacher, patient with less technical users
  • Able to see the whole account, not just the ticket in front of you

Who you might be

  • Someone who worked the Genius Bar at an Apple Store and misses solving problems for a person, not a queue
  • Someone who learned support at a company known for it, such as Basecamp, Automattic, or Help Scout
  • A hotel or hospitality professional who moved into software and kept the instincts
  • A former municipal or deputy clerk who was always the one who figured out the software. You already know our clients' world
  • Or maybe none of these! If the rest of this page sounds like you, we certainly want to hear from you

This is not the job for you if

  • You would rather work a queue than talk to people
  • You find non-technical users frustrating
  • You want to hand a problem to a developer and move on
  • You need someone to tell you what to do next

Work style

  • Independent and ownership-driven. You do not need heavy oversight to perform
  • Comfortable wearing several hats across products and brands
  • Comfortable in a lean, documentation-first team
  • Proactive rather than reactive with accounts

What success looks like

  • Clients describe working with us as a great experience
  • No client has to ask who is handling their problem. They already know it is you
  • Issues you file get fixed without a developer asking for more detail
  • Tickets stop recurring, not just get answered
  • Help center articles created or improved every week, and Fin resolving more each month
  • Repeat questions turned into product fixes or automation
  • Expansion and renewals tied to the accounts you touch
  • Account relationships that are trusted, not just responsive
  • The rest of the team gets better because you are on it

Requirements

Experience

  • Five or more years in technical support or support engineering at a software company, working directly with engineers
  • An issue tracker used daily: Linear preferred, Jira or similar is fine
  • Intercom or similar support tooling, including work with an AI support agent
  • A knowledge base you wrote that other people relied on
  • AI tools such as Claude already part of your daily work
  • Nice to have: government or municipal software, WordPress-based websites, hospitality or other service-first work
  • Able to travel within the US a few times a year. Not required, but very helpful to understand our customers better.

How to apply

  1. Apply through Workable. You will answer two short questions in writing and record a two-minute Loom video teaching us one thing
  2. Complete the Culture Index survey. You can do it right after you apply. We only review candidates who have completed it
  3. Interview with our Head of Client Success
  4. Paid take-home exercise built from real client situations
  5. Conversation with our CTO and founder, including a short role-play call with a clerk who needs help
  6. Offer letter, if selected

Benefits

  • Salary of $85,000 to $105,000 a year, depending on experience
  • 20 paid vacation days, plus public holidays for your country of residence
  • Fully remote, working Central US hours
  • Internet stipend
  • Gym membership or wellness stipend

We do not offer a health plan or a 401(k) today. The salary range reflects that.

The Customer Success Manager (CSM) is responsible for driving adoption, value realization, renewal, and expansion within a defined portfolio of customers. You will act as the primary post‑sales relationship owner, orchestrating the right resources across Support, Product, Services, and Sales to ensure customers achieve their desired outcomes and view us as a strategic partner.

Key Responsibilities

1. Customer Outcomes & Revenue

  • Own customer health, retention, and risk management for your portfolio, in partnership with Sales and Renewals.

  • Build and maintain strong, trust‑based relationships with day‑to‑day contacts, project owners, and business sponsors.

  • Capture and share customer feedback, ensuring issues are followed through to resolution and learnings are socialized internally.
  • Identify and develop customer advocates for references, testimonials, case studies, and events.

  • Keep customer records accurate and up‑to‑date in CS tools and CRM (health scores, notes, success plans, risks, and actions).

Required Experience & Skills

  • Experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Consulting, or similar customer‑facing role in B2B SaaS / enterprise software.
  • Proven track record managing a portfolio of mid‑ to large‑enterprise customers and delivering against retention targets.
  • Strong understanding of subscription / recurring revenue models and the drivers of churn and expansion.
  • Ability to engage confidently with technical and non‑technical stakeholders (from admins to Director/VP level).
  • Comfortable working with data and dashboards (usage, health, NPS/CSAT) and turning insights into clear actions.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and storytelling skills.
  • Strong organization and time management, with the ability to prioritize across multiple accounts and workstreams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in Identity & Access Management (IAM), security, or adjacent enterprise SaaS.
  • Hands‑on experience with Customer Success platforms (e.g., Gainsight, Totango, ChurnZero) and CRM (e.g., Salesforce).
  • Experience running QBRs/EBRs and building structured success plans.
  • Exposure to working with distributed / global teams.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

The Customer Success Manager will be measured on a combination of:

  • Renewal Rate for assigned accounts.
  • Net Revenue Retention (NRR) / expansion pipeline influenced or sourced.
  • Portfolio health: average health score, coverage and freshness of success plans, 
  • Strategic Touchpoint Delivery - EBR’s, Value Unlocks, Road Maps, Success Plan Reviews..
  • Customer advocacy and satisfaction: NPS/CSAT scores, references, and participation in marketing/customer programs.
  • Operational excellence: data quality in systems, timely updates, and adherence to core CS processes.

Behaviours & Values

  • Data‑informed: uses metrics and evidence to guide decisions and prioritization.
  • Collaborative: works openly with peers and partners, sharing information and removing silos.
  • Accountable: owns commitments, communicates proactively, and follows through.
  • Growth mindset: seeks feedback, learns quickly, and adapts to change.

For over 10 years, New Law Business Model (NLBM) has been on a mission to liberate lawyers from outdated, soul-crushing practice models. We provide the heart-centered framework—Life & Legacy Planning®—and the high-octane membership products required to build thriving, relational firms. With a community of 800+ Personal Family Lawyer® firms nationwide, we leverage elite AI and automation to amplify humanity, delivering the practical education, tools, and "done-for-you" systems lawyers need to reclaim their time and build a lasting legacy. We obsess over real-world outcomes, not just vibes, to ensure our members move from survival mode to true flourishing.

The Mission

This Solutions Engineer role independently troubleshoots, maintains, and improves the technology and systems that power Accelerator. You’ll investigate complex technical problems, determine root causes, test and implement solutions, document the work, explain technical concepts clearly, and help create repeatable solutions that reduce recurring issues over time.

 

You are a systems navigator, technical troubleshooter, educator, and client advocate who gets the details right while meeting overwhelmed users with patience and clarity.

 

This role requires ownership, curiosity, patience, and a genuine desire to help people succeed—not simply close tickets.

Job requirements

What You’ll Do

Pillar 1: Member Support, Troubleshooting & Education

  • Own complex technical troubleshooting from discovery through resolution, including root-cause analysis, testing, implementation, documentation, and follow-through.

  • Meet members where they are technically, turning complex issues into clear, approachable guidance through Loom, email, phone, or whatever channel works best.

  • Help members understand not just what to do, but why it matters, so they feel confident handling similar situations in the future; coordinate with external partners and maintain full accountability through resolution. 

Pillar 2: Accelerator Platform & Systems Operations

  • Administer and support the Accelerator technology environment across GoHighLevel, HubSpot, Asana, and connected systems, including the relationships between HubSpot firms, orders, contracts, Asana implementation projects, and Accelerator member accounts.

  • Complete approved account builds, updates, pauses, reactivations, migrations, and technical closeout tasks while troubleshooting workflows, pipelines, calendars, forms, permissions, and settings.

  • Investigate deliverability, phone/SMS, domains, DNS, integrations, and data issues; maintain accurate records and provide bounded support for related legacy platforms as assigned.

Pillar 3: Quality Assurance, Integrations & AI-Assisted Work

  • Use AI thoughtfully and approved integration tools to investigate issues, interpret errors, and complete member requests.

  • Verify recommendations and changes against actual system settings, reliable documentation, and realistic test scenarios.

  • Investigate APIs, webhooks, authentication, logs, and field mappings; coordinate complex development needs, document results and limitations, and protect confidential member information.

Pillar 4: Documentation, Knowledge Sharing & Improvement

  • Learn, document, and progressively take ownership of recurring technical processes.

  • Document technical knowledge so teammates can work confidently and apply repeatable solutions.

  • Identify patterns across recurring technical issues and recommend repeatable fixes, documentation, automation, or product improvements.

     

What Success Looks Like

  • Members receive accurate solutions, timely updates, clear next steps, and greater confidence using the technology that supports their firms.

  • Technical requests are handled with strong ownership and reliable follow-through, while changes are tested, reviewed, documented, and implemented thoughtfully.

  • Recurring issues lead to better instructions, reusable solutions, or system improvements that teammates can access and apply confidently; you identify problems early and help move members from frustration to forward momentum.

     

Who You Are

  • You have hands-on experience administering and troubleshooting GoHighLevel and HubSpot across multiple accounts, including workflows, order forms, contracts, client records, and support tickets.

  • You understand workflows, pipelines, snapshots, calendars, forms, permissions, account configuration, and the dependencies between shared systems and firm-specific customizations.

  • You are a patient, compassionate teacher who explains technical concepts in plain language and can guide clients through solutions over Loom or Zoom.

  • You understand APIs, webhooks, authentication, JSON, logs, data mapping, email, phone/SMS, DNS, and calendar integrations; you use AI responsibly, document as you go, share knowledge, and own follow-through.

Helpful additional experience includes law-firm or professional-services operations, estate planning, Keap, Lawmatics, Make, Zapier, n8n, data migrations, reconciliation, or light JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python.

 

Compensation & Benefits

  • Position Type: Full-Time, Non-Exempt (W2) 40 Hours / Week

  • Hourly Base Wage: Pay Rate: $40.87–$45.67 ($85,000 – $95,000 / annualized)

    • Starting base pay is determined by factors including geographic location, applicable experience, skills, and internal equity. Non-exempt employees are eligible for overtime pay in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

  • Work Schedule & Compliance: Requires minimum (4) hours core schedule to overlap with Pacific Time (e.g., 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM PT)

Why Join NLBM? 

  • 100% Remote Work at a Profitable, Growing Company

  • Recession-Proof Industry, Product, and Audience

  • Comprehensive Benefits Package (Health, Dental, Vision)

  • 401K Retirement Program

  • Flexible Paid Time Off

  • Opportunities for Career Growth and Leadership Development

  • Be Part of a Mission-Driven Company Transforming the Legal Industry

 

At NLBM, you’ll have the opportunity to make a lasting impact, scale your career in leadership, and be part of a passionate, supportive team driving innovation and change.

 

This role operates under a Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) model. Employees are expected to provide their own computer and internet connection, meeting minimum requirements (including at least 16GB RAM) to perform work duties. The company provides required software and system access, and reimburses reasonable and necessary business expenses including a monthly internet/technology allowance as required by law.
